brief: UBS sales commentary across three regions, each a separate thesis. US: the dollar has been bid for a fourth straight day as market-implied pricing of about 48bps for the December and January Fed meetings now matches UBS Economics' call for two consecutive hikes. SOFR whites repriced sharply, with reds/greens shifting back to levels from a month ago after a period decoupled from US growth and instead tracking oil. UBS expects October PPI at +6.6% y/y (final demand) and +5.0% y/y (core), both post-2022 highs, driven by goods and energy; the broader rates selloff has likely paused since SOFR rate-vol uncertainty hit levels seen in prior stress episodes. Canada: FX is largely ignoring local macro data amid the broad dollar bid; USDCAD has ranged 1.39-1.43 most of the year, and a soft Canadian CPI print would push it past 1.43 since the US-Canada rate differential is already the widest of the year and could widen further. Eurozone: Q3 GDP confirmed at +0.4% q/q / +1.3% y/y; EURUSD hasn't broken 1.10 but cleared 1.11, yet UBS's trend model flags it as the group's weakest trend performer.
